claims.text: TC4 (Ti6Al4V) has a conventional unmodified alpha-plus-beta dual-phase microstructure.
TC4 specimens will be treated by plasma nitriding.
The proposed plasma-nitriding condition is approximately 700 degrees Celsius for 2 hours in a nitrogen-rich atmosphere.
The specified treatment can confine the nitrided layer to a depth of a few micrometers.
Plasma nitriding will produce a nanostructured surface layer predominantly composed of TiN.
The nitrided surface layer may also contain Ti2N precipitates.
Nitrogen diffusion during plasma nitriding induces in situ formation of hard nitride phases.
Nitrogen introduced by plasma nitriding causes interstitial solid-solution strengthening in the near-surface region.
Nitride formation and near-surface solid-solution strengthening increase surface hardness.
The hardened surface produced by nitriding improves wear resistance.
A surface-limited nitriding treatment leaves the ductile alpha-plus-beta core microstructure unmodified.
Plasma-nitrided TC4 will have significantly greater surface hardness than untreated TC4.
Under optimized conditions, the surface-hardness improvement may approach or exceed 50 percent.
Plasma-nitrided TC4 will exhibit a lower wear rate than untreated TC4 in standard wear tests.
Plasma-nitrided TC4 will retain bulk tensile strength and ductility similar to those of untreated TC4.
Untreated TC4 has relatively low surface hardness and high wear rates under high-contact-stress conditions.
The expected benefit applies primarily where surface wear is the critical failure mode.
Keeping the nitrided layer only a few micrometers deep is necessary to avoid compromising bulk properties.
The experiment compares nitrided and untreated TC4 using microhardness, pin-on-disc wear, yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and elongation measurements.
The hypothesis is falsified if nitriding fails to deliver the specified hardness and wear improvements while preserving bulk tensile properties.
